summary: Defines the notation used to state what a management implementation must support and what it actually does support. This helps describe minimum requirements and the level actually achieved. It was replaced by RFC 2580.

eli5.summary: Like a checklist on a product box saying what features are required and which ones this one has. It gives the language for writing such checklists for network management.

questions: what is an snmp object group
how do mib modules describe compliance
subtitle: The notation SNMPv2 uses to say what a MIB module requires of an implementation and what an agent actually supports.

tldr.problem: It is useful to define the acceptable lower bound of an implementation of a MIB module, along with the level of implementation an agent actually achieves, but there was no standard notation for either.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 1904 defines four ASN.1 macros: OBJECT-GROUP and NOTIFICATION-GROUP to bundle related items, MODULE-COMPLIANCE to state minimum requirements, and AGENT-CAPABILITIES to describe what a particular agent supports.
tldr.outcome: Standard MIB modules must have a matching compliance statement. RFC 1904 is a Draft Standard that was obsoleted by RFC 2580.

facts.label: Status values for groups and compliance

today: RFC 1904 is a Draft Standard that has been obsoleted by RFC 2580, which now holds the conformance statements for SNMPv2. It obsoleted RFC 1444.

sections.title: Defining Conformance
sections.content:
A MIB module is a collection of managed objects that an agent exposes to a management station. It may be useful to define the acceptable lower bound of implementation, along with the actual level achieved. RFC 1904 defines the notation for both purposes, as part of the SNMPv2 framework.

There are four macros. The two group macros bundle related items. MODULE-COMPLIANCE says what an implementation must support to claim compliance with a MIB module. AGENT-CAPABILITIES says what a specific agent really supports. Like the textual conventions in RFC 1903, the macros are expanded conceptually during implementation and not at run time.
sections.eli5: There is one tool for packing related items into bundles, one for writing the minimum rules, and one for a product to say what it can really do.

sections.title: Object Groups and Notification Groups
sections.content:
The OBJECT-GROUP macro defines a collection of related managed objects. To implement an object, an agent must return a reasonably accurate value for retrieval and, if the object is writable, be able to influence the underlying entity. An agent that cannot implement an object must return an exception such as noSuchObject. It must never return a value for an object it does not implement.

Every object in the group must be defined in the same module and have a MAX-ACCESS other than not-accessible, and every such object in a module must be in at least one group. This catches the common mistake of adding an object and forgetting to put it in a group. The NOTIFICATION-GROUP macro does the same for notifications. Both carry a STATUS of current, deprecated or obsolete, a DESCRIPTION and an optional REFERENCE, and their value is an object identifier naming the group.
sections.eli5: A group is a labeled box. Everything related goes in one box so you can say "you need box number 8" instead of listing every item.

sections.title: Compliance Statements
sections.content:
MODULE-COMPLIANCE conveys the minimum implementation requirements for one or more MIB modules. Every standard MIB module must have a compliance statement, either in the same module or a companion one.

A MODULE clause names each MIB module. Inside it, MANDATORY-GROUPS lists groups that must be fully implemented. An agent that returns noSuchObject for an object in a mandatory group, or cannot generate a listed notification, is not conformant. GROUP clauses name groups that are conditionally mandatory or optional, with a description of the condition. A group in neither clause is unconditionally optional.

OBJECT clauses refine the requirement for one object with a narrower SYNTAX, a WRITE-SYNTAX for writes, or a MIN-ACCESS. An implementation complies if its access level is at least the minimum and no more than the maximum in the OBJECT-TYPE definition.
sections.eli5: A compliance statement is the rule list for earning a badge: these boxes are a must, these only if you also do something else, and the rest are up to you.

sections.title: Agent Capabilities
sections.content:
AGENT-CAPABILITIES lets an agent implementor describe the precise level of support an agent claims, and bind that description to an instance of sysORID. A management station can keep a database of these statements, read the sysORID values from an agent, and look up matching entries to tune its behavior. The macro describes variations on OBJECT-TYPE and NOTIFICATION-TYPE definitions, not on compliance statements.

The PRODUCT-RELEASE clause describes the product release. Each SUPPORTS clause names a MIB module, and its INCLUDES clause lists the groups the agent implements. VARIATION clauses name objects or notifications that behave differently. They may refine SYNTAX or WRITE-SYNTAX, lower the ACCESS (the value not-implemented means the item is absent), list CREATION-REQUIRES columns that must be set before a row becomes active, or give a different DEFVAL. Each variation needs a DESCRIPTION.
sections.eli5: If compliance is the rule list, capabilities is the product sticker that says exactly which rules this product follows and where it does things a bit differently.

sections.title: Changing a Published Module
sections.content:
Section 10 of RFC 1902 defines how an information module may be extended. RFC 1904 adds one rule for each of its constructs: if any non-editorial change is made to a conformance group, a compliance definition or a capabilities definition, the object identifier value must change, along with its descriptor.

This means a name always points to exactly one set of requirements. Anyone who claims compliance with a named group or statement refers to a fixed definition.
sections.eli5: If you change what is in a box, it gets a new box number, so nobody mixes up the old box with the new one.

items.title: OBJECT-GROUP
items.text: Bundles related managed objects into one unit of conformance.

items.title: NOTIFICATION-GROUP
items.text: Bundles related notifications into one unit of conformance.

items.title: MODULE-COMPLIANCE
items.text: States the minimum a MIB module implementation must support.

items.title: AGENT-CAPABILITIES
items.text: Describes what a particular agent really supports, with variations.
